resources.string: Reads the screen aloud with customizable gestures, low-latency background event handling and a plugin system based on scripts.
Tap the switch to open Accessibility settings, choose \"%1$s\", then turn the service on or off.
Couldn\'t open Accessibility settings on this device. Open them manually: Settings → Accessibility.
The element is no longer on screen
Swipe to choose an item first
Menu is open. Swipe to choose, double-tap to run.
This element has no identifier, so it can\'t be labeled
Nothing to read on the screen
No text found on the screen
The element is too small or off screen
Couldn\'t read the text on the screen
This screen is protected, the app isn\'t allowed to capture it
Too fast, try again in a second
The service doesn\'t have permission to capture the screen
Image with content not yet translated: %1$s
Open menu of the selected element
Copy text of the selected element
Read selected element character by character
Describe image of the selected element
Finds and taps the Skip button for ads on the current screen.
Each rule needs at least one of: text, contentDescription, viewId, className
id may only contain a-z, 0-9, _ and at most 40 characters
match must be contains or equals
action must be click, long_click, focus, scroll_forward or scroll_backward
id \"%1$s\" clashes with a built-in plugin
Turn on the service, battery, permissions
Haptic only, sound only, both, off
Note when installed outside Google Play
Android may grey out the service switch. In that case go to Settings → Apps → %1$s → ⋮ → Allow restricted settings, then turn the service on.
Turn off any other screen reader before use, because both use touch exploration mode.

The accessibility service is kept running by the system and needs no separate background service. Some phones (Xiaomi, Oppo, Vivo, Samsung…) still stop apps to save battery. If the service turns off unexpectedly, set the app to unrestricted battery use.
Currently: the app is NOT battery-restricted.
TTS engine, currently %1$s. Tap to change

Changing the engine takes effect immediately for the running service. The app only uses voices installed on the phone and never sends text over the network. Install a voice for your language in the chosen engine.
Hello, this is the reading voice.
The app interface and spoken messages follow this language. The voice reads in the same language, so install a matching voice.
Couldn\'t open language settings. Open Settings → System → Languages → App languages.
Short feedback when focus moves, at the start/end of a list, or on tap. Turning it on or off here does not affect speech.
Light tick when moving between elements, strong at the limit, click on tap.
Short tick when moving; low tone at start/end; high tone on tap.
To switch quickly while in use, assign \"Change haptic and sound mode\" to a gesture, or pick it from the general menu.
Reads the app name and a shortened text; skips duplicates and merges bursts.
When an app doesn\'t label a button, the reader handles it in this order, without taking screenshots:
1. The app\'s own label (description, text, linked label, tooltip).
3. Text of the child elements inside the button.
4. A guess from the technical name, for example \"btn_close\" becomes \"close\", announced as \"guessed label\".
5. Nothing found: reads \"button, no label\" so you can still tap it.
Open \"Gestures\" to assign: Read text on screen (OCR), Describe image of the selected element and Label the selected element. The first two take a screenshot that is processed on the phone.
Touch the screen with one finger to hear that element. Swipe right/left to move between elements. Double-tap anywhere to tap the element you just heard.
Most gestures can be reassigned in \"Gestures\".

Only Accessibility (which you turn on yourself) and Vibration. The app asks for no network, contacts, location, microphone or storage permission. Scripts loaded from a file use the system file picker, so no storage permission is needed.
OCR uses ML Kit\'s Latin-script recognizer: it reads Latin text well, but accents may be wrong with small or blurry text, and other scripts (Chinese, Arabic, Cyrillic) are not recognized.
\"Describe image\" only lists recognized objects (about 400 kinds, in English, translated where possible) and does not write full sentences.
Android blocks screenshots on secure screens (passwords, banking).
Android doesn\'t let an accessibility service capture edge swipes or drawn characters.
Translations were produced by machine and have not yet been reviewed by native speakers; please report wording problems.
The app\'s own actions are added at the end. Text editing items appear only in input fields.

Label buttons the app forgot to name: select the button, then use the gesture assigned to \"Label the selected element\" (see Gestures). The label is remembered for that exact button every time you open the app.
%1$s, currently %2$s. Tap to change the function
Enabled plugins run when you use the \"Run enabled plugins\" action (it has no default gesture: open it from the menu, or assign a gesture in Gestures).
Plugin \"%1$s\" will be removed from the device and this can\'t be undone.
Couldn\'t read the file, or it is too large (max 64 KB)
This element is not a text field
Off: only says \"character entered\". On: reads each character you type, so people nearby may hear it.
On: adds position and tips (for example \"1 of 13\" in menus). Off: reads names only.
Read text in the selected image
This script does not list any app, so it will run in every app. Install only if you trust it.
See which gestures the system sends to the app
While the test is on, each gesture is only announced by name and nothing is run. If a gesture is not announced, the system did not send it to the app.
Test is on. Do a gesture to hear its name.
No gesture is assigned. Assign one in Gestures.
Reading text from images is not available for this language on this device.
Off by default. Only when you select an image with no label, its text is read on this device. Results can be wrong, and verification images are not reliably readable.
After this change no gesture will be left for “%1$s”, and you may not be able to use the screen. Change anyway?
On: emoji are read by name (for example “face with tears of joy”). Off: the voice decides, and often skips them.
Detailed focus on. Controls the app hides from accessibility, such as an unlabeled checkbox, can now be reached.

On: also reaches controls the app hides from accessibility (for example a checkbox next to terms text). Adds extra stops and can be slower. Off by default; you can also switch it from the menu or a gesture.
Read technical info of the element
Class %1$s. Clickable: %2$s. Checkable: %3$s. Important for accessibility: %4$s. ID: %5$s
Activated the control next to it
Open the element menu to describe the image or read its text.
Records gestures, scrolling and tap attempts (no on-screen text) so problems can be traced. Stays on this device; copy it to send.
To read the names of places near you, the app needs to know your location. Location is only used while this feature is on.
To find people in your contacts, the app needs to read the contacts on this device. You can decline and still use the other features.
You have not granted this permission, so that feature is unavailable for now. You can grant it again at any time in Settings.
This permission has been turned off. To use the feature, open the app\'s Settings and grant the permission.
Permissions are only used while the related feature is on. Turn the feature off and the app stops using that permission.
No feature needs a permission right now. The app asks for no permission at install or first launch.
On: after an element, also read the action to take (for example: Double-tap to activate). Off by default. Independent of Read guidance.
Choose how much is read for each element while browsing. The element\'s own text is always read in full.
Detailed: also the position in a list
Reached the top of the page
Reached the bottom of the page
Sets all four swipes of this group at once. You can still change each swipe below.
Whole page: top or bottom of page, first or last element
Read by unit and turn pages
View or share error logs for technical support
Saves only technical error details inside the app\'s private storage, never anywhere else. Keeps at most 3 crash reports and one short event list, about 70 KB in total. Nothing is sent by itself.
The log holds no screen content, only error types, code locations and app version. Check it before sharing.
No voice for %1$s is installed, so speech may sound wrong. Install voice data in the text-to-speech settings.
The speech engine has no voice for the app language, so text may be read with the wrong voice. Install the voice data to fix this.
Couldn\'t open voice data settings. Open Settings → System → Languages → Text-to-speech.
Choose one engine, or two engines that each read a different language.
Text in this language is read by the second engine; everything else by the first.
Each engine needs its own voice data installed. English and Vietnamese are told apart by the shape of each word, so very short or unusual words may go to the wrong engine.
How to split text between the engines
By word: switches engine at every word of the other language. By sentence: each whole sentence is read by one engine, the one whose language has more words in it; smoother, with fewer voice changes.
Which language the first engine reads. The default follows the app language.
On: on the keyboard, slide to a key to hear it, then lift your finger to type it. Off by default; double-tap still works. Starting a swipe cancels typing.
How long your finger must rest on an element before it is read. 0 reads immediately; a higher value avoids reading everything you slide past.
Give one app its own gesture set
Gestures set here replace the general ones only inside that app. Everything you do not change follows the general gestures.
No app has its own gestures yet.
A finger is on the screen
Skipped while you touch the screen, so they do not cut into what you are exploring.
Skipped during phone and voice calls.
Skipped while the system Do Not Disturb filter is active.
Skipped while music or video is playing.
One word or phrase per line. A notification containing any of them is never read. Ignores case and accents.
One word or phrase per line. A notification containing any of them is always read, even when notification reading is off or a quiet situation applies. The never-read list wins.
Save or restore all settings in a file
Saves your settings, gestures, per-app gestures and custom labels in a text file stored wherever you choose. It does not include extensions, the error log or the speech engine choice.
Settings in the file replace the current ones. Settings not in the file stay as they are.
This is not a valid backup file.
Could not read or write the file.
Tap the screen directly in this app
Activating sends a real touch at the center of the element instead of an accessibility click. Use it for apps where activating does nothing.
Another screen reader is turned on. Two at once can make speech and gestures conflict; turn one of them off.
Short pop-up messages such as Saved are read aloud, even when notification reading is off. On by default.
Alt or Windows/Search plus an arrow key moves between elements; Alt+Enter activates; Alt+Backspace goes back; Ctrl alone stops speech. Other keys type as usual. Full list in Help. On by default.
The chosen speech engine is unavailable. Using the default engine.

Hold Alt (or the Windows/Search key) and press: Right or Left arrow = next or previous element; Down or Up arrow = scroll forward or back; Page Down or Page Up = next or previous page; Home or End = first or last element; Enter or Space = activate; Shift+Enter = long press; Shift+Right or Shift+Left = move by character, word or line; Shift+Up = change that unit; H or Shift+H = next or previous heading; K or Shift+K = next or previous link.

Also with Alt: Backspace = back, Shift+Backspace = Home, R = recent apps, N = notifications, Q = quick settings, M = global menu, L = local menu, T = read from the top, Shift+T = read from the current element, Z = repeat last speech, F = search the screen, S = time and battery, O = read the screen by OCR, D = describe the focused element, C = copy its text. Pressing Ctrl alone stops speech.
Pause or resume keyboard and volume keys
Turn volume-key navigation off or on for this app
Speech always stops when the screen turns off. On: also say Screen off and Screen on. Off by default.
When a dialog or bottom sheet opens, read its title and move to its first element, unless you already chose something. On by default.
When you come back to a window you left, move to the element you were on, if it is still there. Off by default.
Say each character as you type it. On by default.
After you type a space or punctuation, say the word you just finished. Off by default.
When you type a capital letter, say Capital before it. Off by default.
After a list stops scrolling, say which items are visible, for example Items 5 to 9 of 30. Off by default.
Drag the selected slider to the end

A short press still changes the volume. Hold a key, or press both keys, to run the actions you assign in Gesture settings. Works only with the screen on and outside calls. Off by default: while it is on, the Android accessibility shortcut (holding both volume keys) does not work with the screen on.
Single press, double press and hold run the actions you assign in Gesture settings. Works only with the screen on and outside calls. Off by default.
When a slider is selected, the scroll gestures change its value instead of scrolling the page. On by default.

Volume keys (turn on in the reading settings; off by default): a short press still changes the volume; hold volume up or down, or press both keys together, to run the actions assigned in Gesture settings. While this is on, Android\'s own accessibility shortcut (holding both volume keys) does not work with the screen on. The headset button works the same way when turned on.
Alt+P pauses or resumes the keyboard and volume keys, and always works, even while paused. Alt+V turns volume-key shortcuts off or on for the current app. These can also be assigned to a gesture.
To say who is calling, the app needs to know when the phone rings and to see the caller\'s number. It uses this only while the feature is on and sends nothing out of your phone.

To say where you are, the app asks the phone for your location only when you ask it to. Turning a position into an address is done by the phone\'s own location service, which may contact its provider over the internet.

When the phone rings, says who is calling. Needs permission to see phone state and call numbers. You are then asked, optionally, for permission to read contacts; if you allow it the contact\'s name is said instead of the number, otherwise only the number. Off by default.
Lets the action Say my current location work (Alt+G, or a gesture you assign). The phone is asked for its position only when you run that action. Needs location permission. Off by default.
Clear all text in the selected field
Incoming call from an unknown or hidden number
Saying your location is turned off. Turn it on in Reading settings.
Could not get your location. Check that location is turned on, go near a window or outdoors, and try again.
You are near %1$s. Accuracy about %2$d meters.
Your position is latitude %1$s, longitude %2$s. Accuracy about %3$d meters. No address is available.
The signal is weak, so this may be inexact.
This is an older position and may be out of date.
Cleared all text in the field. You can restore it.
The field already has text, so nothing was restored
Calls, location and clearing a field

Incoming calls can be announced by number, or by contact name if you also allow reading contacts (one switch, off by default; permissions are asked only when you turn it on). Say my current location (Alt+G, or a gesture you assign) reads the address and how accurate it is; in Reading settings turn it on first. Clear all text in the selected field is Alt+X, and Alt+Shift+X restores what was just cleared if the field is still empty. Password fields are never cleared or remembered.

In Voice, choose \"both engines\" so one engine reads the app language (for example Vietnamese) and the other reads a second language (for example English). Text that mixes the two is split by word or by sentence and read in turn, never overlapping. The \"switch voice mode\" gesture toggles quickly between one and two engines. Language detection is a best guess: proper names and very short words may be read with the wrong voice.
System gestures with two or three fingers

Two-finger swipes up, down, left and right are passed to Android as ordinary swipes, like in other screen readers: they scroll the content or turn pages on their own. With gesture navigation turned on: swipe up from the bottom edge with two fingers to go Home (swipe up and hold for recent apps), swipe in from the left or right edge with two fingers to go Back, and swipe down from the top edge with two fingers to open notifications. A three-finger swipe up from the bottom edge belongs to Android\'s accessibility button, so the three-finger reading gesture works only when it starts higher up. These gestures cannot be reassigned.
Two-finger swipes are handled by Android, as in other screen readers (scroll and turn pages; system gestures from the screen edges), so they cannot be assigned here.
Reading controls (one-finger swipe up or down)

Swipe down with one finger to move forward and swipe up to move back, by the selected reading control. It starts as one element at a time. Swipe up then down (or swipe down with three fingers) to switch to the next reading control, and swipe down then up (or swipe up with three fingers) to switch to the previous one; the app says the name of the new control. The controls form a circle: element, character, word, sentence, paragraph, heading, controls, link, speech rate. With character, word, sentence or paragraph, when the element\'s text runs out the app moves on to the next or previous element. With headings, controls or links, it jumps to the next or previous one of that kind. With speech rate, swipe up to speak faster and swipe down to speak slower, ten percent at a time. In a text field, swiping down or up moves the real cursor by the selected unit (one character at a time at first) and reads the text it passed over; at the start or end of the text, the next swipe moves to the next or previous element. In a password field, swiping only moves to the next or previous element. When a slider is selected, swipe up to increase and swipe down to decrease. In menus, swiping up or down moves between items like swiping left or right. The \"Change reading unit\" action still works and the reading control follows it. To scroll the page, swipe up or down with two fingers. The reading control goes back to one element at a time when a new window opens. Every one of these gestures can be reassigned in Gestures.
Play or pause music or video
Change reading control and turn pages (default)

Swipe up then left: Home. Swipe down then left: Back. Swipe left then up: Recent apps. Swipe right then down: Notifications. Swipe down then right: General menu. Swipe up then right: Element menu. Swipe left then down: Find text on screen. Two-finger tap: stop speaking. Two-finger double-tap: play or pause music or video. Two-finger triple-tap: read from the selected element. Three-finger tap: General menu. Three-finger double-tap: copy the text of the selected element. Three-finger triple-tap: paste into the text field. Three-finger double tap and hold: cut the text in the text field. Three-finger swipe down or up: change the reading control. Every gesture can be reassigned in Gestures, where you can also restore the defaults.
